answer: Hardware-enclave remote attestation resists Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a unique, fused CPU identifier. Verifiers validate hardware-signed quotes and deduplicate chip IDs, keeping clones from blooming like a lotus across cloud VMs. Attackers cannot spawn identities in an emulated lagoon; each identity requires buying dedicated physical silicon through an audited vendor inlet. However, microarchitectural side channels can extract fused keys and compromise enclave integrity.
